technique: letting one plain object carry the feeling
lesson:
Here is the one technique for today. You take a single ordinary thing and let the whole feeling sit inside it, instead of telling us the feeling directly.

See where the poem does this. "The coffee cup you set down after midnight / is right there still." Then "a cold ring in the bottom." Then "the spoon gone dull beside it." The poem does not say the man is tired or that time has passed. It shows one cup that nobody cleaned.

Here is why that works on you as a listener. A cold cup is a thing you have seen. You know what it means without being told. So you feel the long night through the cup, and you trust it, because it is real and small.

Try this: pick one object near you, describe it in plain words, and let it stand for the mood instead of naming the mood.

The second time through, listen for how the cup gives way to the fence and the bucket, and how all of it leads up to the last words.

Here is the poem.
poem:
The coffee cup you set down after midnight
is right there still, a cold ring in the bottom,
the spoon gone dull beside it. You forgot it,
the way a man forgets a thing he settled—
all that counting done in rooms not his,
names stacked against names, the long math of strangers.
Out here the numbers thin to something plainer:
one fence that needs its wire pulled taut again,
one bucket, one boot, one hand that does the pulling.
The window's going pale at the far edge now,
the hills resolving back into themselves,
indifferent to the tally, keeping theirs—

Whatever the long night counted, morning keeps its own quiet tally—and the first thing on today's list is simply to be here for it—

So — up!
